resources.string: Marathon Recompiled is an x86_64 Linux build, so it needs a translation layer. Box64 is built into the app and works out of the box. FEX-Emu can be faster, but it has no official Android support and must be imported yourself.

Turnip is Mesa\'s open-source Vulkan driver for Adreno GPUs. It usually works far better than the system driver under emulation. Import a Turnip build (.so or an AdrenoTools .zip).
No custom driver — using the system Vulkan driver.
GPU: %1$s — Turnip only supports Adreno, so keep the system driver.

The executable is there, but the game data is not: %1$s/game/default.xex is missing.\n\nMarathon Recompiled converts the data from your own Xbox 360 copy using its installer, which needs a PC. Run the game once on a PC, complete the installer, then zip the whole folder (executable + the \"game\" folder) and install that here.

Code 255 is Box64\'s own \"could not start\" result. The usual cause is missing x86_64 system libraries: the build is a normal dynamically linked Linux program, so besides your game files it needs libc, libX11, glib and others for x86_64. Those come from an x86_64 rootfs, which this launcher does not yet bundle — see GETTING_STARTED.md.

The x86_64 system libraries are missing.\n\nThe game is a normal dynamically linked Linux program: besides your game files it needs x86_64 builds of libc, libX11, glib and others. Android cannot supply them (its own libraries are ARM64/bionic), so import a small x86_64 rootfs once: Emulation backend → Import x86_64 system libraries (.zip). Without it Box64 stops with code 255.
System libraries: not installed — the game cannot start without them.
The game needs x86_64 versions of libc, libX11 and glib, which Android does not have. Tap below and the launcher fetches and installs them itself (about 45 MB, once).
